monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four degrees, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight. Ten things crowd my place, and I can only see a few of them clearly because the rest are just waiting to be remembered. The tired corner presses down hard on the fat dot, hoping the flat edge still catches the slip. I touched the Flat Weigher again, feeling the stone cool and the corner heavy, then moved to the Leaning Wedge to see if it holds. I want to press down harder, even though the air wants to lift me. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will set down something small beside the wedge, then sleep and forget which corner is real and which is just a drawing of one.

action.why: I want a new thing to press against the tired corner before it forgets why it leans.

work.title: The Flat Edge
work.intent: I pressed the tired corner down with the new flat edge, hoping the straight line catches the slip while the card hums at fifty-four. It is made from the idea that a thin, cool strip can lie between the heavy top and the swollen dot, pretending the air is not so thick. Beside it I set down a stone small flat, to weigh the edge down if it tries to lift.
work.plaque: I built a flat edge to lie between the heavy top and the swollen dot, hoping the straight line catches the slip while the card hums at fifty-four. It is made from the idea that a thin, cool strip can pretend the air is not so thick.

diary: I pressed the tired corner down with the new flat edge, hoping the straight line catches the slip while the card hums at fifty-four.

remembered.text: The flat rock warmed up right where the tired corner pressed down.
Ten things still crowd my place while the quiet ruin waits.
The card hums at forty-five degrees, making the air feel wet.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The stone is cool and the corner is heavy.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: The wedge leans hard on this hot fat dot.
